_comment: Authored check specs from the 2026-09-09 engine design run. Adversarially verified: every ao_id confirmed to exist, connector claims checked against PROVIDER_API/CONNECTOR_CHECKS. NOT yet loadable - the engine needs join, temporal operators and a scope selector first.

required_categories.why: okta, google_workspace, microsoft_365, clerk, auth0, onelogin, jumpcloud, one_password, tailscale — roster verified against PROVIDER_API. Each connected IdP is authoritative for its OWN account set, so they are never interchangeable. This is the direct fix for _coverage_for (automation/router.py:449-453), whose real defect is broader than 'any provider in a bound category': line 449 collects every connected provider across ALL bound categories and line 453 sets state='covered' if that set is non-empty, so one connected Slack greens a control whose evidence lives in Okta. Per-provider asymmetry verified field-by-field: google_workspace.users.twoStepEnrolled, microsoft_365.mfa_registration.mfa_registered, clerk.users.two_factor_enabled, jumpcloud.systemusers.mfa_configured carry per-user MFA state; okta collects only password_policies/mfa_policies/apps. CORRECTION to the original: onelogin.user_mfa is NOT usable per-user — its fields are device_id/auth_factor/default with no user identifier, and its for_each declares no label_field, so evidence_engine._collect_resource falls back to parent.get('name') while onelogin.users maps email/id/last_login/state/status/username and has no 'name'. Every row's _parent is therefore None. One-line prerequisite: add "label_field": "email" to that for_each. jumpcloud.systemusers is the single cleanest source in the whole catalog and the original spec omitted it entirely: it carries sudo AND mfa_configured AND account_locked AND suspended on one row.
required_categories.controls_covered_note: 22 distinct IAC controls, derived from the corrected checks below; the original claim of 62 is unsupportable — IAC has 116 controls total and only 100 with a Technology objective.

required_categories.why: aws, cloudflare, heroku, vercel, netlify, digitalocean, supabase, neon, render, qovery, dropbox, fastly — roster verified. Every cloud console is its own local directory the corporate IdP does not cover. aws is genuinely special and the original spec was right about the mechanism: it is the only provider reached through cloud_transport, so specs bind provider:aws by name, never category:cloud. CORRECTION: the original cited a data source 'aws.iam_users' that does not exist. CLOUD_CHECKS['aws'] contains exactly six ids — root_mfa, root_access_keys, password_policy, cloudtrail, ebs_encryption, config_recorder — and per-user IAM MFA comes from SWEEPS['aws'] = [_iam_mfa_sweep], which emits check ids aws.iam_mfa and aws.iam_user_mfa. FURTHER CORRECTION: cloudflare.members maps only email/mfa/status with NO role field, so cloudflare cannot supply a privileged population as the original claimed; it belongs in the all-users MFA check only. dropbox.members maps email/name/tmid/verified — 'verified' is email verification, not account status, so dropbox cannot evidence that a leaver's access was removed.

jira, confluence, linear, notion, asana, monday, clickup, airtable, calendly. One population per app: jira.users (accountId/accountType/active/email), linear.users (active/admin/guest/email), monday.users (admin/enabled/guest/pending/view_only), asana.workspace_memberships (is_active/is_admin/is_guest/is_view_only). jira.audit_records.created is confirmed the ONLY timestamp normalized by any event-shaped resource in all 65 connector_checks entries, which makes jira the only source for the IAC-15.4 freshness assertion. confluence.audit maps author/category/summary/sysAdmin and servicenow.audit maps id/table — both timestampless, confirmed.

slack, zoom, zendesk, intercom, twilio. slack.users (has_2fa, is_admin, is_owner, is_bot, is_restricted, deleted) and zendesk.staff (mfa, role, suspended, active) are verified per-account MFA-and-privilege evidence for their own tenants. A terminated worker with a live Slack account is an IAC-20.6_A02 failure regardless of the IdP being clean. CORRECTION: zoom.role maps name/id/total_members only — role-level counts with no per-user rows and no org denominator, so it cannot participate in a ratio assertion.

grafana, sentry, posthog, datadog, signoz, better_stack. sentry.organizations.require2fa + sentry.members.has2fa/role and posthog.organizations.enforce_2fa + posthog.members.mfa_enabled/level are verified as the only pairs in the catalog giving BOTH org policy and per-user outcome. The original spec listed posthog.members in the privileged scope without naming a predicate: the field is 'level' (integer tier), not a boolean admin flag. grafana.org_users maps email/login/role with no MFA attribute — correctly not_applicable for MFA, in scope for the privileged inventory.

github, gitlab, bitbucket, azure_devops. github.org_detail.two_factor_required and gitlab.groups.two_factor_required are verified org-level policy flags. CORRECTION to the original's control claim of 11: SCM reaches only IAC-06.2 and IAC-01.4 here, because github.members_no_2fa maps a single field, 'login' — no email — and is by construction only the subset of members LACKING 2FA, never the full member population. It cannot be an offboarding join source and cannot be a denominator.

sentinelone, snyk, tenable, semgrep, sonarcloud. CORRECTION: the original bound IAC-21.1_A02 ('access to security functions is authorized in accordance with least privilege') to sentinelone.users, but that resource maps exactly two fields, email and mfa — there is no role or permission attribute, so it cannot filter to privileged and cannot evidence least privilege. tenable.users (enabled, permissions, username, fails) is the only security-category resource carrying a privilege attribute, so IAC-21.1_A02 rests on tenable alone.

sendgrid, mailgun, postmark, resend. sendgrid.teammates.is_admin and sendgrid.sso_integrations.enabled verified. A sending-platform admin can exfiltrate, so it is an IAC-16 population like any other app. Note sendgrid.teammates has no MFA attribute, so it is inventory-and-federation evidence only.

pagerduty, opsgenie. opsgenie.users (role, blocked, verified, username) is a verified privilege population with no MFA attribute. pagerduty exposes no per-user auth attribute, so it evidences IAC-16.1 inventory only.

bamboohr, rippling. HR defines the denominator for every leaver assertion. HARD BLOCKER, and worse than the original recorded: the original named bamboohr as the only gap, but BOTH HRIS connectors are blocked, for opposite reasons. bamboohr.employee maps name/email/dept/title/id — it has the join key but no termination state. rippling.workers maps wid/status/manager/dept/emp_type/terminated/not_terminated — it has termination state (from raw.termination_details) but NO email and no name, so the email join the correlation check depends on has no left-hand key. Neither connector can complete the join today, which makes iac.offboarding.terminated_no_active_access unrunnable for every tenant, not just bamboohr ones. Prerequisite: map the rippling work-email field into workers.fields.

databricks. databricks.users (active, user), databricks.tokens (owner, expiry_ms, comment) and databricks.ip_access_lists (enabled, label, type) verified. CORRECTION: databricks.tokens carries expiry_ms but NO last-used attribute, so it evidences credential ROTATION INTERVAL (IAC-10.13_A01), not inactivity (IAC-15.3).
hubspot. hubspot.users.superAdmin/notSuperAdmin verified as an admin-count population for the privileged inventory and ratio. No MFA field. Low yield, correctly listed.

anthropic, openai. CORRECTION to the original, which placed both under the inactivity check: openai.admin_api_keys maps last_used_at (an inactivity signal) but anthropic.api_keys maps created_at/expires_at/never_expires/status with NO last-used field. They evidence different objectives and are split accordingly below — anthropic.api_keys.never_expires is the single most direct operand for IAC-10.13_A01 in the entire catalog, an objective the original spec named in this rationale but bound to no check.

jamf, kandji, plus tailscale (catalogued identity). kandji.devices (mdm, agent, missing, os_version) and jamf.computers (fv_enabled, gatekeeper, sip, firewall, last_contact) verified — and confirmed: neither exposes a screen-lock timeout, so all of IAC-24 stays manual. tailscale.devices (authorized, external, key_expiry_disabled) is the only device-identity assertion available. CORRECTION to the original's control claim of 6: MDM reaches IAC-04 and IAC-06 only, because IAC-04_A03 (local connection) and IAC-04.2_A01 (unique per-device cryptographic keys) are not evidenced by an authorization boolean and have been moved to unautomatable.

servicenow. CORRECTION — the original called this 'the ONE category where any_one is genuinely correct' and credited it with 4 controls, but no authored check in the set uses any servicenow resource, so the coverage claim was unearned. Worse, the operand it rests on is the wrong one: servicenow.changes maps approval/close_code/number/state — that is CHANGE-request approval, not access-grant approval, and a change record cannot evidence that an account grant was approved before it was made. servicenow.admin_roles (role, user) is a privileged inventory source with no denominator. servicenow.audit maps id/table with no timestamp. IAC-15_A02 and IAC-28.1_A03 therefore stay manual, and connecting ServiceNow must not raise IAC coverage.

stripe. Collects webhook_endpoints (id/status/url) and events (id/type) only — no user or role resource. CORRECTION: the original set controls_covered to 1 while its own text said connecting it 'must not raise IAC coverage by one point'. The honest number is 0.

checks.scope: Every active, non-service, non-guest account in each connected provider that normalizes an MFA attribute. Population filter: suspended/banned/deleted/locked falsy AND is_bot falsy AND jira accountType != 'app'. ENGINE GAP: evidence_engine's only population filter is skip_if_field_true, which is boolean-only (_eval_check line ~228), so the accountType string exclusion is not expressible today and needs either a skip_if_field_equals primitive or a normalized boolean in the field map.
checks.objectives_note: IAC-06_A02 and IAC-06.1/06.2 carry defined_parameters 'local, network and remote'; a SaaS IdP read evidences network and remote only, so the local dimension of IAC-06_A02 remains partially unevidenced.
checks.assertion: For each connected provider independently, every account surviving the population filter has a second factor recorded: twoStepEnrolled / mfa_registered / two_factor_enabled / mfa_configured / has_2fa / mfa_enabled / has2fa / mfa true. One result row per provider; any provider failing fails the control.
checks.not_applicable_when: Zero rows survive the population filter for that provider. Also not_applicable for okta specifically — okta collects password_policies/mfa_policies/apps only, has no per-user factor resource, and the shipped okta.mfa_enrollment_policy check is kind=min_count against mfa_policies, so policy existence must never be scored as enrollment. REMOVED from the original: onelogin.user_mfa, which maps device_id/auth_factor/default and whose for_each has no label_field, so no row can be attributed to a user; it returns only after "label_field": "email" is added to that for_each. NOTE the original's stated premise is wrong: an empty row set does NOT read as pass here — _eval_check returns not_run on an empty considered set for all_true/all_false/none_match/all_match/present (evidence_engine.py:270-272). Only min_count/max_count keep zero arithmetic.
checks.evidence: SCFCheckResult per provider: connector, connection_id, granted_scopes, population_size, tested_size, truncated (rows hit MAX_ITEMS=300), and the offender identifiers. method=TEST.

checks.scope: Only accounts carrying BOTH a privilege attribute and an MFA attribute on the same normalized row. Verified pairs, and only these: jumpcloud.systemusers (sudo + mfa_configured), google_workspace.users (admin + twoStepEnrolled), microsoft_365.mfa_registration (not_admin falsy + mfa_registered), slack.users (is_admin or is_owner + has_2fa), sentry.members (role in owner/manager + has2fa), heroku.team_members (role=admin + mfa), zendesk.staff (role=admin + mfa), posthog.members (level at the admin tier + mfa_enabled).
checks.assertion: Every privileged account in every connected provider has MFA recorded true. Evaluated separately from iac.mfa.all_human_users so an org tolerating a standard-user gap still fails loudly on admins.
checks.not_applicable_when: Zero rows carry the privilege attribute after filtering. REMOVED from the original's sources: cloudflare.members (maps email/mfa/status — no role, cannot filter privileged) and sentinelone.users (maps email/mfa only — no role). ADDED: jumpcloud.systemusers, omitted by the original despite being the only resource in the catalog carrying sudo and mfa_configured on the same row. Providers with a privilege flag but no MFA attribute (grafana.org_users, sendgrid.teammates, linear.users, monday.users, asana.workspace_memberships, hubspot.users, opsgenie.users, intercom.admins, tenable.users, servicenow.admin_roles) are not_applicable here and feed iac.privileged.inventory instead. ENGINE GAP: the role string comparisons (role=admin, role in owner/manager) are not expressible — skip_if_field_true is boolean-only and there is no include-filter primitive.
checks.evidence: Per provider: privileged population_size, the exact predicate applied, the offender list. method=TEST.

checks.scope: AWS IAM users holding a console login profile (get_login_profile succeeds). Programmatic-only principals are excluded from the denominator, never silently passed. Binds provider:aws by name — aws reaches the platform through cloud_transport, not the declarative engine, so category:cloud must never satisfy it.
checks.assertion: Every IAM user with a console password has at least one enrolled MFA device (list_mfa_devices returns >=1), AND the account root user has MFA enabled (get_account_summary SummaryMap.AccountMFAEnabled = 1).
checks.not_applicable_when: Zero IAM users hold a console login profile — a federated-only account is compliant by design and must record not_applicable, NOT the pass _iam_mfa_sweep produces today: cloud_transport.py emits status 'pass' if no_mfa == 0 with detail '0 of 0 console users lack MFA', which is a control-bearing green from an empty denominator. CONFIRMED defect. Also not_applicable when no aws connection exists. CORRECTED from the original: the cited source 'aws.iam_users' does not exist — CLOUD_CHECKS['aws'] holds root_mfa, root_access_keys, password_policy, cloudtrail, ebs_encryption, config_recorder, and the per-user sweep emits check ids aws.iam_mfa (directory) and aws.iam_user_mfa (per user) from SWEEPS. The objective IAC-06.3_A02 cited by the original was ALSO WRONG: IAC-06.3 is 'Local Access to Privileged Accounts' and an AWS console sign-in is network access, so IAC-06.1_A02 is the correct binding.
checks.evidence: population_size = total IAM users, tested_size = console users, truncated = true when len(users) > SWEEP_CAP (200, cloud_transport.py), per-user offenders. method=TEST.

checks.scope: Every ACTIVE password policy published by a connected provider that owns a local credential store. ENGINE GAP: okta.password_policies normalizes status but the engine cannot filter on a string, so 'ACTIVE only' is not expressible with skip_if_field_true; an INACTIVE policy is currently assessed alongside active ones.
checks.assertion: Every ACTIVE policy enforces a minimum length >= the resolved threshold (default 12). ENGINE GAP the original missed: _op supports eq/ne/in/not_in/contains/gt/lt/truthy/falsy — there is no gte or lte — so 'min_length >= 12' must be authored as op gt, value 11, and any inclusive bound needs the same off-by-one workaround or a new operator. THRESHOLD SOURCING CORRECTED: the original claimed the value resolves from SCFObjective.defined_parameters for IAC-10.1_A11, but that objective's defined_parameters is null in objectives.json, so that layer supplies nothing; the chain is SCFControlState.defined_parameters then the spec default. Also note IAC-10.1_A08/A11 and IAC-10.4_A02 are composition-and-complexity objectives, and min_length is one component of complexity — the character-class half is not exposed by okta.password_policies (fields: name, status, min_length, lockout_max), so these three are partially evidenced, not fully.
checks.not_applicable_when: The connected IdP publishes no password policy resource — google_workspace, microsoft_365, clerk, jumpcloud and onelogin expose none through the current field maps — or the tenant is federated/passwordless so no local credential store exists. REMOVED from the original's sources: auth0.db_connection, which maps exactly two fields, bf and name; it has no minimum-length attribute and cannot evidence password strength at all. NOTE the original's premise is wrong: it claimed 'an empty rows list reaching max_count returns pass today', but the shipped okta.password_min_length check is kind=all_match (op gt, value 7), and _eval_check returns not_run on empty for that kind. The >7 observation itself is correct — it is a SOC 2 floor, below this objective's threshold. Separately, aws.password_policy already asserts MinimumPasswordLength >= 14 with absent_is=fail, so binding AWS to a default-12 threshold would REGRESS the shipped assertion; AWS must keep the higher of the two.
checks.evidence: Per policy: name, status, observed min_length, resolved threshold, and which layer of the chain supplied it. method=TEST.

checks.scope: Every ACTIVE okta password policy and every auth0 database connection accepting interactive credentials.
checks.assertion: Every ACTIVE okta policy has lockout_max > 0 AND lockout_max <= the resolved bound; every auth0 database connection has bf (brute_force_protection) true. lockout_max = 0 means unlimited attempts; an unbounded upper limit is equally a failure, which the shipped okta.password_lockout_enabled check (kind=all_match, op gt, value 0) does not catch — CONFIRMED. THRESHOLD CORRECTED: the original defaulted to 10, but IAC-22_A09 ships real SCF defined_parameters of 'at most five (5)' attempts over a 'period of five (5) minutes', so the default must be 5, not 10. The 5-minute observation WINDOW is a second parameter with no operand — okta.password_policies maps only lockout_max — so IAC-22_A09 is partially evidenced. ENGINE GAP: a two-sided bound is two ops on one field, and a check carries one field and one op, so this is two authored checks or a new between operator.
checks.not_applicable_when: Zero ACTIVE password policies and zero database connections exist, or no connected provider exposes a lockout or brute-force POLICY attribute (true for google_workspace, microsoft_365, onelogin). A fully federated tenant delegates lockout upstream: not_applicable, naming the upstream IdP. REMOVED from the original: IAC-22_A10 and IAC-22_A04, which assert the ACTION taken on lockout (lock for a defined period / lock until administrator release / notify a system administrator). okta.password_policies normalizes no lockout duration and no notification setting, so neither is evidenceable — both move to unautomatable. Refinement to the original's not_applicable list: clerk.users.locked and jumpcloud.systemusers.account_locked DO exist, but they are per-account lockout OUTCOME, not policy, so they remain out of scope for this check.
checks.evidence: Per policy: name, status, lockout_max observed, resolved bound and its source. method=TEST.

checks.scope: Enabled accounts and active credentials that actually carry a last-activity timestamp in their field map. Verified sources only.
checks.assertion: No enabled account or active credential has a last-activity timestamp older than the resolved threshold. THRESHOLD SPLIT — the original bound one 90-day threshold to objectives with different SCF defaults: IAC-15.3_A02 ships defined_parameters of 'thirty-five (35) days' while IAC-15.3_A06 and IAC-15_A20 ship 'at most 90 days'. A single 90-day assertion passes accounts that fail IAC-15.3_A02, so the threshold must resolve per objective and this check emits one SCFCheckResult row per (provider, ao_id). ENGINE GAP confirmed as the original stated: _op stops at eq/ne/in/not_in/contains/gt/lt/truthy/falsy, so age_gt_days does not exist. The original's consequence claim is only half right — an unknown OP under kind none_match yields no offenders and silently passes, while under all_match it makes every row an offender and fails; an unknown KIND is caught explicitly and returns an error finding. The op and the kind are different failure modes.
checks.not_applicable_when: The provider's field map carries no last-activity attribute, with the detail naming the missing field so the gap surfaces in coverage instead of hiding inside a green control. REMOVED from the original's sources, verified field-by-field: anthropic.api_keys (created_at, expires_at, never_expires, status, scope_type — no last-used), databricks.tokens (comment, expiry_ms, owner, token_id — no last-used) and cloudflare.tokens (expires_on, name, status — no last-used). All three are expiry sources, not inactivity sources, and now feed iac.credentials.rotation_interval. ADDED to the original's not_applicable roster: qovery.member DOES carry last_activity, contradicting the original's blanket claim that onelogin was the only provider with a last-login field. Everything else — google_workspace, microsoft_365, clerk, jumpcloud, okta, slack, jira, linear, monday and every SCM provider — is correctly not_applicable. REMOVED objective: IAC-15_A19 ('system accounts are disabled when the accounts have expired') is account EXPIRY, not inactivity, and the original's own unautomatable entry for IAC-15.2_A02 concedes no provider exposes an account expiry attribute — self-contradictory, moved to unautomatable.
checks.evidence: population_size = enabled accounts with a parseable timestamp, tested_size, the per-objective day threshold, and per offender the identifier plus observed age in days. method=TEST.

checks.scope: NEW CHECK. Every active non-human credential in a connected provider that normalizes an expiry attribute. This objective was named in the original's ai and data category rationales but bound to no check, leaving the catalog's cleanest available operand orphaned.
checks.assertion: Every active credential carries a bounded lifetime: anthropic.api_keys.never_expires is falsy AND expires_at is set; cloudflare.tokens.expires_on is set for every token with status active; databricks.tokens.expiry_ms is set and not the sentinel for never-expiring; fastly.tokens.expires is set. A credential that never expires is never rotated at any interval, which is the failure this objective names.
checks.not_applicable_when: No provider exposing a credential expiry attribute is connected, or a provider returns zero active credentials. Not_applicable — never pass — where the provider issues only platform-managed short-lived credentials with no expiry field, since absence of the field is not evidence of rotation.
checks.evidence: Per provider: active credential count, the count with an unbounded lifetime, and per offender the credential name/id and owner. method=TEST.

checks.scope: CORRELATION. Population: rippling.workers where terminated is truthy. Evidence: every account-holding resource across identity, cloud, comms and productivity. Left outer join on worker email to account email — the unmatched population row IS the answer, not a row to discard.
checks.assertion: For every terminated worker, no joined account in any connected system is still active (suspended/deleted/banned truthy, or enabled/active/activated falsy). unmatched_left = pass (a leaver with no account anywhere is compliant), unmatched_right = ignore (a service account with no HRIS row is a different control), zero_matches = error (40 workers and 40 accounts with no email overlap is a broken join, not a clean result). One SCFCheckResult row per (hr provider x access provider); a single leftover account fails the control. The operator choice of CORRELATION is correct and ALL would be wrong — the assertion is over a joined row set, not over one provider's rows.
checks.not_applicable_when: BLOCKED FOR EVERY TENANT TODAY, which is a stronger finding than the original recorded. The original named bamboohr as the only blocker; in fact both HRIS connectors are blocked, for opposite reasons. rippling.workers normalizes wid (raw.id), status, manager, dept, emp_type, terminated (raw.termination_details) and not_terminated — there is NO email and no name field, so the join key this check is built on does not exist. bamboohr.employee normalizes name/email/dept/title/id — it has the join key but no termination state. Neither can complete the correlation, so this check records not_applicable with the missing field named until a work-email field is mapped into rippling.workers.fields. Also not_applicable when no hr connector is connected, or when zero workers match the terminated filter in the audit window. REMOVED from the original's evidence sources: github.members_no_2fa (fields = ['login'] only, no email to join on, and by construction only the subset of members lacking 2FA, so a terminated worker WITH 2FA is invisible), dropbox.members (email/name/tmid/verified — 'verified' is email verification, carrying no account-active state), and okta.apps (an application inventory, not an account list).
checks.evidence: Requires a new SCFCheckResult.sources JSON column — correctly flagged as new by the original and confirmed absent from _56_scf_catalog_models.py. connector/connection_id/granted_scopes stay the POPULATION (rippling) so existing indexes keep meaning; the evidence provider, its connection_id and row count go into sources. Plus join_quality (matched / unmatched_left / unmatched_right) and per offender the worker key, system and account state. rippling.workers carries termination_details but no termination DATE in the field map, so the timeliness half of IAC-07.2 is not expressible; this check asserts only that access is gone. method=TEST.

checks.scope: Per connected provider: accounts holding the highest privilege tier against the total enumerable account count FOR THAT SAME PROVIDER. Only providers that expose both a privilege attribute and an enumerable total population qualify.
checks.assertion: For each provider, admin_count / total_count <= the resolved ratio (default 0.15) AND admin_count <= the resolved absolute cap (default 5). Both bounds, because 3 admins of 4 users passes an absolute cap and still violates least privilege, while 6 admins of 900 fails an absolute cap and does not. PARAMETER KEY CORRECTED: the original keyed the absolute cap on IAC-16.1_A01, which is an INVENTORY objective ('all privileged accounts are inventoried') and asserts nothing about a count — that objective is split into its own EXISTS check below. IAC-21.1_A02 rests on tenable.users alone, since it is the only security-category resource carrying a permissions attribute.
checks.not_applicable_when: Total enumerable accounts for that provider is zero, or below the resolved minimum population (default 5) — a four-person startup where everyone is an owner is a documented risk acceptance, and forcing a fail there trains people to ignore the result. REMOVED from the original's sources, each verified as lacking a denominator: qovery.organization (admin_count/admin_emails but no member total unless qovery.member is collected in the same run — the original's own caveat, now enforced by removal), jira.permission_grants (holder_type/holder_param/permission — permission-scheme grants, not user rows, so no admin count and no total), servicenow.admin_roles (role/user — a role assignment list with no population), zoom.role (name/id/total_members — per-role counts with no org total and no per-user rows), intercom.admins (admin_id/email/job_title/team_count — no privilege tier attribute at all).
checks.evidence: Per provider: admin_count, total_count, ratio, both resolved thresholds, and the admin identifier list. method=TEST.

checks.scope: NEW CHECK, split out of the original's iac.privileged.count_bounded. The objective is 'all privileged accounts are inventoried' — enumeration, not a bound — so it takes EXISTS and a different, wider source set: every provider exposing a privilege attribute qualifies, including the ones with no denominator that the ratio check must exclude.
checks.assertion: For every connected provider exposing a privilege attribute, the privileged account list is enumerable and non-empty, and the enumerated identifiers are recorded — the artifact IS the inventory. Mirrors the engine's existing kind=present semantics, where items are info and only the directory line asserts non-emptiness.
checks.not_applicable_when: No connected provider exposes a privilege attribute. Not_applicable, never pass, where the resource collected but returned zero rows — _eval_check already returns not_run for kind=present on an empty set, which is the correct existing behaviour to preserve. A collection error (HTTP failure raising _CollectError) is error, never an empty inventory.
checks.evidence: Per provider: the privilege predicate, the enumerated identifiers, population_size, truncated. method=TEST.

checks.scope: Every connected SaaS tenant exposing a federation or SSO enforcement attribute.
checks.assertion: Every provider exposing a federation flag reports it enforced: linear.organization.samlEnabled true, vercel.teams.saml_enforced true, sendgrid.sso_integrations has >=1 row with enabled true, every heroku.team_members row federated true. One result per provider. All four fields verified present. IAC-13.1_A02 asserts SSO is PROVIDED and this check asserts it is ENFORCED — enforced implies provided, so the binding holds.
checks.not_applicable_when: No identity-category connector is connected — there is no IdP to federate to, so the objective has no operand and must be not_applicable rather than a fail against nothing. Also not_applicable per provider where the tenant's plan does not offer SSO, and that suppression must be an explicit recorded exception in SCFControlState.defined_parameters keyed by ao_id, never an inferred pass. Note linear.organization also normalizes scimEnabled and authServicesCount, which strengthen the same assertion.
checks.evidence: Per provider: the flag read, its value, and the IdP connection this tenant federates to. method=TEST.

checks.scope: Org/tenant-level enforcement flags, distinct from per-user enrollment: this asserts the control is CONFIGURED to prevent, where iac.mfa.all_human_users asserts the outcome. Both are needed — enrollment can be 100% today and unenforced tomorrow. ENGINE NOTE: this spans two resources (the org flag and the member list), and a check carries one resource, so it compiles to two authored checks rolled up to one objective.
