checks.not_applicable_when: DROPPED NET-12_A01 from objectives. NET-12 is titled 'Safeguarding Data Over Open Networks' but its single assessment objective reads 'approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources are enforced in accordance with applicable access control policies' — an access-control assertion, not a cryptographic one. Binding a TLS test to it claims something the objective does not say, and the objective text is what an assessor reads. Route NET-12_A01 to the IAC/access-control domain instead. Otherwise: not_applicable when the connected provider publishes no internet-facing endpoint (zero sites / zones / load balancers). Cloudflare zones with status != 'active' are excluded from the population (cloudflare.zones already collects 'status').
checks.evidence: Endpoint hostname + the failing setting value (e.g. min_tls_version=1.0), per provider.

checks.scope: Every internet-facing zone/project/load balancer across all connected cloud providers.
data_sources: vercel.projects.firewall_enabled (EXISTS: bool:security.firewallEnabled, backed by vercel.project_firewall_enabled all_true)
cloudflare.zone_rulesets (NEW: /zones/{id}/rulesets, phases http_request_firewall_managed + http_ratelimit, fields phase, enabled, rules_count)
aws.waf_associations (NEW: wafv2.list_web_acls + list_resources_for_web_acl — list_ passes the read-only guard)
checks.assertion: Every internet-facing zone/project/load balancer has an enabled managed firewall ruleset AND at least one rate-limit rule (the DoS half of NET-02.1_A04).
checks.not_applicable_when: The provider exposes no edge firewall capability at the tenant's plan tier (Cloudflare free plans return no managed ruleset — an entitlement fact, not a control failure; record the entitlement, mirroring supabase.network_restrictions.entitlement which is already collected). Also not_applicable when the provider serves zero internet-facing endpoints. A zone that returns a rulesets list containing zero enabled rules is FAIL, not not_applicable — that is the same null/empty-vs-absent distinction the supabase _op defect gets wrong.
checks.evidence: Zone/project id, ruleset phase, enabled flag, rate-limit rule count, plan tier.

checks.scope: Every active zone in the connected Cloudflare account (named provider — DNS authority is not substitutable).
data_sources: cloudflare.zones (EXISTS — fields name/status/id, confirmed in connector_checks.json)
cloudflare.dns_records (NEW: /zones/{id}/dns_records?type=TXT, fields name/content/type; a for_each child of the existing zones resource, which the engine already supports)
checks.assertion: For each active zone, exactly one apex TXT record starting 'v=spf1' exists and its terminal mechanism is '-all' or '~all' (not '+all', not '?all', not absent).
checks.not_applicable_when: OPERATOR CORRECTED from EXISTS to ALL: the assertion is universally quantified over every active zone, and EXISTS would let one correctly-configured zone green an account holding ten unprotected ones. Otherwise: not_applicable when no cloudflare connection; OR zone status != 'active' (Cloudflare is not authoritative, so its record set is not the truth); OR the zone is flagged non-sending in tenant parameters. Multiple v=spf1 records at the apex is a FAIL (RFC 7208 permerror), not not_applicable. Zero records returned for an active zone is a collection failure, not a pass.

checks.scope: Every active Cloudflare zone that publishes SPF (i.e. every sending domain).
checks.assertion: A _dmarc TXT record exists and its p= tag is 'quarantine' or 'reject'. p=none is a FAIL — a monitoring-only policy does not authenticate incoming email, which is what NET-20.4_A01 asserts.
checks.not_applicable_when: No cloudflare connection; OR zone status != 'active'; OR the zone is a parked/non-sending domain per the tenant's declared sending-domain parameter. A missing _dmarc record on a sending zone is FAIL, never not_applicable — absence is the finding.

checks.scope: Every active Cloudflare zone.
checks.assertion: DNSSEC status is 'active' for every zone — signing enabled AND the DS record published at the parent, which is what makes the chain of trust verifiable (NET-10_A04) rather than merely signed (NET-10_A01).
checks.not_applicable_when: REMOVED NET-18.5_A01 and NET-18.5_A02. NET-18.5 is 'Domain Name Verification' and its objectives read 'internal/external domain name LOOKUPS are validated according to DNSSEC' — that is the RESOLVER side (your recursive resolvers validating signatures on other people's zones). Cloudflare zone DNSSEC is the AUTHORITATIVE side (signing your own zone so others can validate). Opposite ends of the protocol; both moved to unautomatable. NET-10_A01 ('additional data origin authentication provided along with the authoritative name resolution data the system returns') and NET-10_A04 (chain of trust) are the correct and sufficient bindings. Otherwise: not_applicable when no cloudflare connection; OR zone status != 'active'; OR the TLD registry does not support DNSSEC (record the reason). status 'pending' — signed but DS not at the parent — is FAIL: the chain is broken.

checks.scope: Every domain registered through the connected Cloudflare account.
data_sources: cloudflare.registrar_domains (NEW: /accounts/{id}/registrar/domains — a for_each child of the EXISTING cloudflare accounts resource, which already collects id and name, so the parent is free)
checks.assertion: Every registered domain has locked=true and auto_renew=true, and expires_at is more than 30 days away.
checks.not_applicable_when: The Cloudflare account registers zero domains (empty registrar list) — the common case where domains are held at a third-party registrar with no connector. Resolves not_applicable AND routes to a manual EXAMINE, never pass: an empty list here means 'we cannot see the registrar', which is the empty-population failure mode. Note the engine's min_count kind would pass an empty set here (it uses len(rows) arithmetic and never returns not_run), so this check must NOT be authored as min_count/max_count — use the offender-list shape, which does return not_run on empty.

checks.scope: Every sending domain on every connected email-category provider (all_connected).
data_sources: sendgrid.authenticated_domains (NEW: /whitelabel/domains — base is https://api.sendgrid.com/v3 so the path resolves; fields domain, valid, dkim.valid, spf.valid)

postmark.sender_domains (NEW: /domains — WARNING: Postmark's /domains endpoint requires the ACCOUNT token, while the existing postmark webhook resource uses a SERVER token. This is a second credential, not a field-map addition. Do not ship it as 'NEW field map' without confirming the connector's stored credential shape.)
checks.assertion: Every sending domain on every connected sender is verified/active — DNS ownership plus SPF and DKIM proven at the provider. One unverified sender fails the control even if every other sender is clean.
checks.not_applicable_when: REMOVED NET-20_A01. Its text is 'an email filtering security service is implemented' — inbound content filtering, not outbound sender authentication. It is NOT unautomatable though: it is already evidenced by mailgun.domains.spam_action, so it moves to net.email.content_filtering_enabled below. Otherwise: an individual email provider with zero sending domains is dropped from the denominator, not counted as a pass. Whole check not_applicable when no email-category connector is connected.

checks.scope: Every sending domain on every connected email provider exposing a filtering policy field.
data_sources: mailgun.domains.spam_action (EXISTS: raw.spam_action, backed by mailgun.spam_filtering none_match eq 'disabled')
checks.assertion: No sending domain has its spam/content filtering action set to disabled — i.e. an email filtering security service is in force on every domain.
checks.not_applicable_when: NEW CHECK, added to give NET-20_A01 the home it actually has rather than deleting a real ao_id. not_applicable when no email provider exposing a filtering policy field is connected (resend, sendgrid and postmark expose none today) or the provider returns zero domains. NET-20_A02/_A03 (attachment detection and blocking) are NOT evidenced by spam_action and stay manual.
checks.evidence: Domain name + spam_action value.

checks.scope: Every sending domain on connected email providers that expose a transport-TLS policy field.
data_sources: postmark.webhook.url (EXISTS: postmark.webhook_https, all_match contains 'https://') — a real in-transit assertion at the webhook boundary; the original spec wrongly said postmark exposes nothing here
checks.assertion: Every sending domain requires TLS on delivery (require_tls true) AND verifies the peer certificate/hostname (skip_verification false). These are two independent checks today whose separate passes let one green the control; the corrected check ANDs them per domain.
checks.not_applicable_when: DROPPED NET-12_A01 (same reason as net.cloud.tls_at_external_boundary — its objective text asserts logical-access enforcement, not cryptography). Otherwise: the connected email provider exposes no transport-TLS policy field — resend and sendgrid do not today — so those connections resolve not_applicable with reason 'field not exposed by provider API', visibly distinct from pass. Also not_applicable when the provider has zero domains.

checks.scope: Every non-external node on the connected Tailscale tailnet (named provider — the ZTNA overlay, not substitutable by another identity connector).
data_sources: tailscale.devices.external (EXISTS: 'isExternal', used as the population filter)
checks.assertion: Every non-external tailnet node is explicitly authorized (device admitted only after authentication) AND has key expiry enforced, so the node key re-authenticates rather than granting standing access.
checks.not_applicable_when: REMOVED NET-01.1_A01 ('all USERS are treated as potential threats and prevent access until the USER can be properly authenticated'). tailscale.devices.authorized is device admission, which is exactly NET-01.1_A02's wording; it says nothing about user authentication. NET-01.1_A01 is rehomed to net.remote.ssh_strong_auth below. Otherwise: not_applicable when no tailscale connection, OR the tailnet returns zero non-external devices. CONFIRMED: tailscale.device_authorized and tailscale.key_expiry_enabled both carry skip_if_field_true 'external', and evidence_engine.py:273-275 already returns not_run on the resulting empty considered set — this spec upgrades that not_run to an explicit not_applicable that leaves the denominator.

checks.scope: Every system managed by a connected JumpCloud tenant.
data_sources: jumpcloud.systems.allow_ssh_password (EXISTS: allowSshPasswordAuthentication, backed by jumpcloud.no_ssh_password_auth all_false)
jumpcloud.systems.allow_ssh_root (EXISTS: allowSshRootLogin, backed by jumpcloud.no_ssh_root_login all_false)
jumpcloud.systems.hostname + .os (EXIST — also a second endpoint population the original spec missed by filing jumpcloud only as an interchangeable IdP)
checks.assertion: No managed system accepts SSH password authentication or direct root login — the user is authenticated by key/MFA before remote access is granted, rather than by a reusable secret.
checks.not_applicable_when: NEW CHECK, added because jumpcloud.systems is already-collected remote-access boundary evidence the original spec overlooked entirely, and it gives NET-01.1_A01 (users authenticated before access) a real home after it was removed from the Tailscale device check. not_applicable when no jumpcloud connection or the tenant returns zero systems. Note jumpcloud is category=identity, so the identity category is NOT interchangeable: no other IdP in it reports host SSH policy.
checks.evidence: hostname, os, allowSshPasswordAuthentication, allowSshRootLogin.

checks.scope: Population = every managed corporate endpoint from every connected MDM (and jumpcloud.systems). Evidence = the Tailscale tailnet node list.
data_sources: POPULATION: jamf.computers.name (EXISTS: raw.general.name) + kandji.devices.name (EXISTS: device_name) + jumpcloud.systems.hostname (EXISTS — third population source the spec missed)
checks.assertion: Every managed endpoint appears as an authorized node on the managed access overlay — remote access is routed through a managed access control point rather than direct to resources. Join mdm.name -> tailscale.hostname; an unmatched endpoint is the FAIL, which is exactly what an inner join deletes.
checks.not_applicable_when: ENGINE GAP, must be recorded on the spec: no CORRELATION kind exists. evidence_engine._eval_check supports only min_count/max_count/all_true/all_false/none_match/all_match/present, and run_connector_checks(provider, spec, creds, base, cdef) collects resources for ONE provider — a cross-connector join cannot be expressed in connector_checks.json at all. This check must live above the connector runner (automation/router aggregation), not in the declarative catalog. Otherwise: not_applicable when no mdm/jumpcloud connector (no population), OR no tailscale connection (no evidence side — not_applicable plus a manual EXAMINE, never a pass). Zero matches across two non-empty sides is ERROR with a join_quality detail: hostname is a weak key (jamf raw.general.name, kandji device_name, jumpcloud hostname, tailscale hostname), and a systematic naming mismatch must be loud, not reported as 100% uncovered.
checks.evidence: Matched/unmatched endpoint names per source, join_quality ratio, coverage_num/coverage_den.

checks.scope: Population = every managed endpoint from every connected MDM. Evidence = whichever agent reports a firewall field for that endpoint.
checks.assertion: Every managed endpoint has its host firewall enabled — the key internal boundary at the device edge. An endpoint in the population with no agent reporting firewall state is uncovered, not passing.
checks.not_applicable_when: OPERATOR CORRECTED from ALL to CORRELATION. The original spec wrote ALL, but its own not_applicable_when described a coverage denominator spanning jamf, kandji and sentinelone — that is a union-join on device name across three independently-collected providers, not a single-population universal. ALL over each provider separately is exactly the shape that hides the gap: jamf.firewall_enabled passes over jamf's own rows while every kandji-only laptop (kandji collects mdm_enabled/agent_installed/is_missing and, in device_details, filevault — VERIFIED: no firewall field) is silently absent from the denominator. Otherwise: an endpoint reported only by kandji and not covered by a SentinelOne agent is not_applicable with reason 'no agent reports firewall state', counted in coverage_den. Whole check not_applicable when neither jamf nor sentinelone is connected. Same engine gap as above: no join kind exists today.
checks.evidence: Per-endpoint name, reporting agent, firewall value; coverage_num/coverage_den split into enabled / disabled / unreported.

checks.scope: Population = managed endpoints from all connected MDMs and jumpcloud. Evidence = SentinelOne agents (NAMED; tenable/snyk/semgrep/sonarcloud in the same category cannot evidence this).
checks.assertion: Every managed endpoint has an active, up-to-date agent capable of revoking or quarantining that host's network access. Join on device name; an unmatched population row (endpoint with no agent) is a FAIL.
checks.not_applicable_when: OBJECTIVE REBOUND: NET-08_A01 removed. Its text is 'Network Intrusion Detection / Prevention Systems (NIDS/NIPS) is utilized to detect and/or prevent intrusions into the NETWORK' — SentinelOne is a host EDR agent, not a network sensor, and asserting NIDS from an endpoint agent roster is the same class of false pass the original spec correctly warned about for Snyk, one tier less obvious. NET-08.3_A01 ('host containment protections exist that revoke or quarantine a host's access to the network') is what SentinelOne actually evidences, and it was named in the spec's own category rationale but bound by no check. NET-08_A01 moved to unautomatable. Otherwise: not_applicable when no mdm/jumpcloud population (an agent list without a fleet list proves existence, not coverage). Zero cross-matches on two non-empty lists is ERROR (name-key mismatch), never 0% coverage. Same engine gap: no join kind, must live above the connector runner.
checks.evidence: Per-endpoint name, agent presence, isActive, isUpToDate; coverage_num/coverage_den.

checks.scope: The tenant's IdP (any_one across okta / microsoft_365 / google_workspace / auth0 / onelogin / jumpcloud).
data_sources: okta.sign_on_policy_rules (NEW, and the original spec's field map was WRONG: Okta session settings do not live on the policy object. Correct shape is a parent resource /policies?type=OKTA_SIGN_ON (fields id, name, status) plus a for_each child /policies/{id}/rules with fields settings.session.maxSessionIdleMinutes, settings.session.maxSessionLifetimeMinutes, settings.session.usePersistentCookie, status. The engine already supports for_each with vars, so the shape is available. VERIFIED: okta's existing connector_checks entry collects only password_policies, mfa_policies and apps — there is no session resource today.)
microsoft_365.conditional_access (EXISTS but collects only displayName + state — sessionControls.signInFrequency is a genuine field-map addition, as the spec said)
checks.assertion: Every ACTIVE sign-on policy rule terminates the session after no more than the tenant-parameterised idle period (default 15 minutes privileged, 60 otherwise), bounds absolute session lifetime, and does not set a persistent cookie.
checks.not_applicable_when: OBJECTIVE CORRECTED: NET-07_A02 replaced with NET-07_A06. NET-07_A02 reads 'terminated at the END of the sessions' — an idle timeout does not evidence end-of-session termination. NET-07_A06 ('terminated at the end of the session OR after an organization-defined time period of inactivity') is exactly what a combined idle + max-lifetime assertion proves. Note THRESHOLD is expressible today as all_match with op 'gt'/'lt' (evidence_engine._op lines 184-192) — it is not a new engine kind, unlike CORRELATION. Otherwise: not_applicable when no identity-category connector is connected, OR the IdP returns zero ACTIVE sign-on policy rules (inactive rules are filtered out of the population). Zero active rules is not_applicable-plus-manual, not pass. NET-07_A04 (termination when nonlocal maintenance completes) and NET-05.2_A06 (internal connection termination) are not evidenced by this and stay manual.
checks.evidence: Policy/rule name, maxSessionIdleMinutes, maxSessionLifetimeMinutes, usePersistentCookie.

domains.domain: NET — Network Security (100 controls, 388 objectives, 206 Technology, 95 controls with ≥1 Technology objective — all four counts reproduced from seed_data/scf/objectives.json + controls.json)

required_categories.why: For NET the boundary IS the cloud account, and each connected provider is its own perimeter, so any_one is wrong and _coverage_for (automation/router.py) is the confirmed defect: it computes `"connected": any(x["connected"] for x in v)` per category and then `state = "covered" if satisfying`, so one connection greens every option in the category. Verified network-boundary fields collected TODAY: supabase.network_restrictions.allowed_cidrs + allowed_cidrs_v6 + entitlement, supabase.ssl_enforcement.enforced, neon.projects.block_public + ip_allowlist_count, digitalocean.firewalls (name/status only) + databases.in_vpc + databases.ssl, netlify.sites.ssl + force_ssl, vercel.projects.firewall_enabled, heroku.apps.acm (the original spec wrongly listed heroku as having no network surface — acm is collected today and consumed by no check). CORRECTED exclusion list: dropbox, render and qovery declare no network resource; heroku DOES (acm); fastly declares tls_activations but maps only the field 'id' with a min_count>=1 check, so it is a presence signal, not a per-endpoint assertion. aws has NO connector_checks entry at all — only the 6 CLOUD_CHECKS in cloud_transport.py (root_mfa, root_access_keys, password_policy, cloudtrail, ebs_encryption, config_recorder), none of them network.

Second, distinct role held by ONE named provider: cloudflare is the DNS/registrar authority. FLAG ON THE SCHEMA ITSELF — 'category' is the wrong key for this row. Cloudflare's DNS authority is a provider-scoped role, not a property of the cloud category, and emitting 'cloud' twice with conflicting semantics means a consumer keying on category cannot resolve which rule applies. The correct encoding is a provider-scoped requirement; this row is kept only because the schema offers no provider field. The DNS family (NET-10.3 SPF, NET-20.4 DMARC, NET-10_A01/_A04 chain of trust, NET-10.4 registrar lock) has exactly one authoritative source per zone. cloudflare.zones is collected today (name/status/id) and cloudflare.accounts (id/name) is collected too, so dns_records, zone dnssec and registrar domains are all for_each children of existing parents — field-map additions, not new connectors. Substituting fastly or vercel proves nothing about a zone's TXT records.

Every connected sending platform is an independently spoofable domain: sendgrid, resend, mailgun, postmark. One unauthenticated sender undoes SPF/DMARC org-wide, so any_one would let a verified Resend domain mask an unverified Mailgun one. Verified collected fields: mailgun.domains {name, state, is_disabled, require_tls, skip_verification, spam_action}; resend.domains {name, status, region, capabilities.sending, capabilities.receiving}. CORRECTIONS to the original: (a) mailgun.spam_action is a real inbound-filtering field the spec overlooked, which is why NET-20_A01 is automatable rather than mismapped-and-dropped; (b) postmark DOES expose a transport assertion today — postmark.webhook_https (all_match contains 'https://') plus has_auth — so the claim that only mailgun has a TLS field is wrong; (c) sendgrid's collected ip_whitelist (/access_settings/whitelist) is a genuine ingress restriction the spec missed; (d) postmark's /domains endpoint needs the ACCOUNT token while the existing webhook resource uses a SERVER token, so it is a credential change, not a field-map addition.

SPLIT OUT of the original single identity row, which the spec's own prose said was two things but its output encoded as one. NAMED providers, not interchangeable: (1) tailscale is the ZTNA/WireGuard overlay for NET-14 remote access and NET-01.1_A02 — devices {name, hostname, os, user, keyExpiryDisabled, updateAvailable, authorized, isExternal} are all collected, and authorized/key_expiry are literally 'device authenticated before access is authorized'. (2) jumpcloud.systems {hostname, os, fde.active, allowSshRootLogin, allowSshPasswordAuthentication, allowMultiFactorAuthentication} is collected today and is remote-access boundary evidence AND a third endpoint population — the original spec filed jumpcloud only as a substitutable IdP and lost both. Substituting okta for either proves nothing about how remote access reaches a host.

The session-policy / conditional-access authority: okta, microsoft_365, google_workspace, auth0, onelogin. any_one AMONG THESE ONLY (a tenant runs one primary IdP), never across the whole identity category — see the evidence_provider row above. microsoft_365.conditional_access is collected today (displayName, state only). CORRECTION to the spec's okta plan: okta's connector_checks entry today holds password_policies, mfa_policies and apps — no session resource — and Okta session settings live on the policy RULE (/policies/{id}/rules, settings.session.maxSessionIdleMinutes / maxSessionLifetimeMinutes / usePersistentCookie), not on the policy object the spec named. Residual risk on any_one: a tenant with both m365 and google_workspace live is issuing sessions from both, and any_one would let the stricter one mask the looser. Acceptable only because forcing all_connected would fail tenants who connect m365 for mail evidence alone.

jamf and kandji define the set of corporate endpoints — the denominator for every host-boundary test and for the EDR/overlay coverage joins. all_connected within the role: both fleets are in scope when both are connected. VERIFIED: jamf.computers collects {name, last_contact, fv_enabled, gatekeeper, sip, firewall} — firewall = raw.security.firewallEnabled, so jamf carries both population and evidence. kandji.devices collects {device_id, name, platform, os_version, mdm_enabled, agent_installed, is_missing} and kandji.device_details adds only filevault — NO firewall field, confirmed. So kandji contributes population without host-firewall evidence, which is exactly why population and evidence must be separate roles, and why net.endpoint.host_firewall_enforced had to change from ALL to CORRELATION.

NAMED, never any_one. sentinelone.agents {computerName, isActive, encryptedApplications, firewallEnabled, isUpToDate, agentVersion} is host EDR / host firewall / containment. tenable {scanners, scans, users} is vulnerability scanning. semgrep/snyk/sonarcloud are static code analysis with zero network relevance. Treating the category as interchangeable lets a Snyk connection satisfy 'NIDS/NIPS is utilized to detect intrusions into the network' — the most dangerous false pass in the domain. CORRECTION beyond the original: sentinelone must not evidence NET-08_A01 either. A host agent roster is not a network sensor; the honest binding is NET-08.3_A01 (host containment), which the spec named in this rationale but bound to no check. NET-08_A01 is now unautomatable.

any_one across datadog / grafana / signoz / better_stack for the 'monitored at the boundary' half of NET-03_A05/_A07 and NET-02.1_A10/_A11, where the strongest truthful assertion remains EXISTS ('a monitoring pipeline is configured') — datadog.monitors and grafana.dashboards are min_count/present only, so no check claims 'network traffic is monitored'. CORRECTION: the spec's blanket 'presence checks only, no real assertion' is wrong. grafana.datasources.tls_skip_verify is collected and asserted (grafana.datasource_tls_verify, none_match eq True), and better_stack.monitors collects {url, monitor_type, status, paused, verify_ssl} with better_stack.monitors_verify_ssl all_true. Both are genuine TLS-verification assertions, and better_stack.monitors.url is an external-endpoint population the spec left on the table.

zoom only, NAMED, for NET-13 electronic messaging / VoIP — and it earns no check today. Collected: zoom.user {email, verified, status, type, role_id}, zoom.role {name, id, total_members}, zoom.managed_domain {domain, status}. No meeting-encryption or VoIP policy field exists, so NET-13_A01 is not assertable and NET-13_A03/_A04 stay manual. controls_covered corrected from 1 to 0: the original row claimed coverage its own rationale then withdrew. slack/zendesk/intercom/twilio carry no network-boundary evidence. Listed for completeness of the category map only.

unautomatable: NET-08_A01 — NIDS/NIPS utilized to detect and/or prevent intrusions into the NETWORK. MOVED HERE from the original spec's net.nids.coverage_on_managed_fleet. SentinelOne is a host EDR agent; a fleet-coverage join over agent rosters evidences endpoint agent deployment, not a network sensor. Binding it to NET-08_A01 is the same false-pass class the spec correctly rejected for Snyk, one tier subtler. Rebound to NET-08.3_A01 (host containment) in net.edr.containment_coverage_on_managed_fleet. No connector in any of the 16 categories collects network-sensor telemetry.

NET-18.5_A01 — internal domain name LOOKUPS are validated according to DNSSEC. MOVED HERE from net.dns.dnssec_enabled. NET-18.5 is Domain Name Verification and asserts the RESOLVER validating signatures on inbound lookups. Cloudflare zone DNSSEC is authoritative-side signing of your own zone — the opposite end of the protocol. No connector collects recursive-resolver DNSSEC validation state.
NET-18.5_A02 — external domain name lookups are validated according to DNSSEC. Same reason; resolver-side, not authoritative-side.

NET-12_A01 — approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources are enforced in accordance with applicable access control policies. REMOVED from both TLS checks. NET-12's control title is 'Safeguarding Data Over Open Networks', but its single assessment objective's text asserts access-control enforcement, and the objective text is the assessable unit. Not unautomatable in principle — it belongs to the IAC access-control domain, not to a NET TLS check. Flagged here so the mismap is not silently reintroduced.

NET-06.5_A01 — Internet access FROM sensitive/regulated data enclaves is prohibited or strictly-controlled. REMOVED from net.cloud.datastore_not_internet_reachable: that check tests INGRESS reachability, this objective is about EGRESS from the enclave. No connector collects outbound/egress rules (digitalocean.firewalls maps name+status only; AWS egress rules would be a new describe_security_groups field), so it stays manual until an egress field map exists.

NET-07_A02 — network connections terminated at the END of the sessions. REMOVED from net.session.idle_timeout_enforced and replaced with NET-07_A06. An idle timeout does not evidence end-of-session termination; nothing in the IdP field maps observes session teardown events.

NET-01.1_A01 was NOT left unautomatable — rehomed to net.remote.ssh_strong_auth on the already-collected jumpcloud.systems SSH fields, after being removed from the Tailscale device check where tailscale.devices.authorized evidences device admission (A02) and not user authentication.

NET-20_A01 was NOT left unautomatable — rehomed to the new net.email.content_filtering_enabled on mailgun.domains.spam_action, after being removed from the sending-domain check where it asserted inbound filtering, not outbound sender authentication.

NET-15.4_A01 — transmission power levels calibrated so wireless signal does not leave controlled boundaries. Physical RF measurement; no connector reports AP transmit power and there is no wireless-infrastructure category among the 16.
NET-15.3_A03 — radio antennas selected to limit signal reception outside controlled boundaries. Hardware procurement decision, evidenced by a purchase/design record.
NET-12.1_A03 — external wireless links protected from signal parameter attacks. RF-layer property; requires spectrum evidence no connector produces.
NET-12.1_A04 — internal wireless links protected from signal parameter attacks. Same reason.

NET-15.5_A02 — rogue WAPs responded to per published incident response plans. Asserts a PROCESS OUTCOME, not a config state; incident-category tickets would evidence that a ticket existed, not that the response followed the plan.
NET-11_A02 — out-of-band channels for physical delivery or electronic transmission of components/devices. Physical logistics; nothing observes courier or OOB transfer.
NET-16_A01 — trust relationships established with other organizations owning/operating intranet systems. An agreement between legal entities; evidenced by a signed document (ERL), not a network read.
NET-02_A01 — security functions implemented as a layered structure minimising inter-layer interactions. Architecture judgement over a design document.

NET-06.2_A01 — VLANs enabled to limit device-to-device communication on a subnet. On-premises L2 switching; no connector reaches switch config. The cloud analogue (security groups) is a different mechanism, covered by net.cloud.deny_ingress_by_default rather than by claiming this objective.
NET-08.1_A01 — DMZ network segments separate untrusted from trusted networks. On-prem topology; the AWS public/private subnet test evidences NET-06_A05/_A10 honestly but is not a DMZ.
NET-06.6_A01 — microsegmentation per application/data workflow. Requires an east-west policy export (service mesh / NSX / Illumio); no connector collects one.
NET-19_A01 — automated Content Disarm and Reconstruction technologies implemented. No CDR vendor among the 66 connectors.
NET-19_A02 — CDR mechanisms configured to detect and remove unapproved active content. Same reason.

NET-20_A02 — email filtering configured to detect malicious attachments. mailgun.spam_action evidences that filtering is enabled (NET-20_A01) but says nothing about attachment detection; no connector exposes an attachment-scanning policy field.
NET-20_A03 — email filtering configured to prevent users accessing malicious attachments. Same reason.

NET-03.3_A01 — discovery of specific system components representing a managed interface is prevented. A negative property about external enumerability; provable only by external scanning, which the read-only connector model deliberately does not do.
NET-09.2_A02 — a unique session identifier generated per session with defined randomness requirements. Application-internal; no SaaS API exposes session-ID entropy.
NET-18.2_A03 — encrypted communications traffic made visible to monitoring tools. TLS-inspection state held in proxy/firewall appliances with no connector.
NET-14_A01 — usage restrictions ESTABLISHED for each type of allowable remote access. Asserts a documented restriction exists, not that a device enforces it. Manual EXAMINE against the ERL row.
NET-14_A03 — connection requirements ESTABLISHED for each type of allowable remote access. Same shape as NET-14_A01.

NET-15.2_A01 — wireless capabilities disabled prior to issuance and deployment when not intended for use. MDM sees the device only after enrolment, so no connector can observe the 'prior to issuance' condition.
NET-10.1_A02 — name/address resolution systems implement internal role separation. On-prem split-horizon DNS architecture; Cloudflare is authoritative-only.
NET-10.1_A03 — name/address resolution systems implement external role separation. Same reason.

NET-20.5_A01 — email systems configured to enable users to digitally sign outgoing email. Automatable in principle from microsoft_365 S/MIME policy, but no connector collects it and inventing the field map without the API contract would be fabrication.
NET-13_A01 — cryptographic mechanisms protect message externals. zoom collects only user/role/managed_domain; no meeting-encryption field exists.
NET-13_A03 — use of VoIP technologies is controlled. Same reason; stays manual rather than being backed by a connectivity pass.
NET-13_A04 — use of VoIP technologies is monitored. Same reason.
NET-07_A04 — network connections terminated when nonlocal maintenance is completed. No connector observes maintenance-session lifecycle.
NET-05.2_A06 — internal system connections terminated after organization-defined conditions. Not evidenced by IdP session policy; no connector reads internal connection state.

domains.domain: MON — Continuous Monitoring (58 controls with Technology objectives, 136 Technology objectives) — verified against grc/seed_data/scf/objectives.json

required_categories.why: CORRECTED from all_connected. The submitted spec declared all_connected and then, in its own caveat, said the checks must name providers because posthog (organizations/members, 2FA fields only) and sentry (organizations/projects/members only) can never satisfy a log-retention or alert-rule test — verified: neither has any log, index, rule or dashboard resource in CONNECTOR_CHECKS. all_connected at CATEGORY level is precisely the bug it warns about: a PostHog-only tenant reads as observability-connected. The evidencing subset is named — datadog (monitors, log_indexes, slos), grafana (dashboards, org_users, service_accounts, datasources), signoz (rules, dashboards), better_stack (monitors, policies) — and each NAMED provider that is connected must pass (a disabled SigNoz rule is not excused by a healthy Datadog).

Unchanged — correct. Each connected AWS account is both population_provider (a system that must be logged) and evidence_provider (its own trail). all_connected because a second account with no trail is a real gap. The blocker is WORSE than the spec stated: aws is the ONLY provider of 66 with no CONNECTOR_CHECKS entry at all (it has transport:aws, no base/verify), so a per-trail collector CANNOT be a declarative connector_checks resource. It must be a row-producing sweep in cloud_transport.py alongside _iam_mfa_sweep, with a per-trail get_trail_status fan-out. get_trail_status does clear the _READONLY_AWS_PREFIXES guard in aws_runner.py. Today CLOUD_CHECKS['aws'] holds aws.cloudtrail as one any_item_field_equals on trailList/IsMultiRegionTrail and aws.config_recorder as one list_nonempty — verified: one boolean per account, no rows, no population_size.

Semantics correct (a tenant runs one on-call system; requiring both pagerduty and opsgenie would fail any org that migrated), but controls_covered CORRECTED from 4 to 0: not one authored check in this set sources from pagerduty or opsgenie. Both do expose the routing-target half without field-map changes (pagerduty: escalation_policies with rule_count, services with has_escalation_policy, oncalls; opsgenie: schedules/enabled, escalations, integrations), so this is a real and cheap expansion — but it may not be counted as coverage until a check binds it.

CORRECTED from all_connected — same substitution bug scf.MON-01.10.idp_log_export_active explicitly guards against in its own not_applicable_when, so the category declaration contradicted the check. Verified: of nine identity providers only auth0 (log_stream: name, status) and one_password (signinattempts:user, auditevents:action, itemusages:user — no timestamp on any of the three, so min_count>=1 is the only expressible assertion) have anything log-shaped. okta, google_workspace, microsoft_365, jumpcloud, clerk, onelogin and tailscale expose no event resource. Under all_connected an Okta-only tenant marks not_applicable and reads as covered.

CORRECTED from all_connected: only 2 of 9 productivity providers carry an audit resource (jira.audit_records, confluence.audit). notion, linear, asana, clickup, monday, airtable and calendly carry none, so all_connected marks them not_applicable and inflates coverage. Within the named pair, every connected one is tested. The domain's most surprising evidence_provider claim VERIFIED by scan of all 66 connectors: jira.audit_records is the only event-shaped resource whose field map retains a timestamp (created). confluence.audit keeps category/summary/author/sysAdmin and drops it; servicenow's sys_audit requests sys_created_on in sysparm_fields and then keeps only sys_id and tablename. The other timestamps in the catalog (anthropic api_keys, twilio keys, fastly tokens, jamf lastContactTime, sonarcloud lastAnalysisDate…) sit on token/user/device resources, not event streams.

Unchanged — correct, and the strongest semantics claim in the set. jamf and kandji define the managed-endpoint denominator for MON-01.6. Without an MDM the EDR-coverage check has no denominator and must report error, never pass on sentinelone's self-reported agent list. Verified ceiling: kandji.devices exposes device_id/name/platform/os_version/mdm/agent/missing and jamf.computers exposes name/last_contact/fv_enabled/gatekeeper/sip/firewall — NEITHER collects a serial number, so the EDR join is hostname-only until kandji serial_number and jamf GENERAL.serialNumber are added.

Unchanged — correct. sentinelone.agents (name, active, uptodate, encrypted, firewall, version) is the only thing in the catalog evidencing host-based monitoring (MON-01.6_A03) and an integrity-verification tool being employed (MON-01.7_A01). Named-provider rather than any_one is right: semgrep, snyk, sonarcloud and tenable are not interchangeable with an EDR, and letting any of them satisfy an EDR-coverage objective is the category-substitution bug in _coverage_for.

controls_covered CORRECTED from 2 to 0. github/gitlab/bitbucket/azure_devops could supply the asset denominator for a logged-asset-inventory test, but no such check exists in this set (MON-02.9_A01 was removed from the CloudTrail check — see below), and verified: no SCM connector collects an audit-log resource. scm supplies a denominator and no monitoring evidence, so it evidences nothing in MON today.

controls_covered CORRECTED from 1 to 0 — the spec's own text said this should not be counted and then counted it. slack's only resource is users.list, so the platform can prove Slack exists and cannot prove one alert was ever routed into it. Documented as a ceiling, claimed as nothing.

checks.scope: Every log index on the connected log platform (datadog.log_indexes). Population = the indexes themselves; each index is a retention bucket and each must independently satisfy the retention parameter.
data_sources: datadog:log_indexes — VERIFIED (path /logs/config/indexes, items:[indexes], fields name, retention_days from num_retention_days)
checks.assertion: sources:[{role:population, provider:datadog, resource:log_indexes, require:named}] assert:{op:ALL, where:[["retention_days","gte",{param:"MON-04_A02", default:365}]]} empty_population:fail
checks.evidence: One SCFCheckResult per connected Datadog org: population_size = index count, tested_size = same, detail lists offending index names and their retention_days. connector=datadog. Strictly stronger than the shipped datadog.log_retention_adequate (gt 7, bound to CC7.2). ENGINE GAP: evidence_engine._op implements eq/ne/in/not_in/contains/gt/lt/truthy/falsy only — gte is a NEW operator, not an existing one. Param has a home: SCFControlState.defined_parameters is JSON 'answers keyed by ao_id'; note MON-04_A02 itself carries no SCF defined_parameters value, so 365 is our default, not an SCF-stated one.
checks.not_applicable_when: No provider in the SIEM role (datadog) is connected for this scope. NOT not_applicable when Datadog is connected and returns zero indexes — empty_population:fail. FIXED: MON-02_A03 removed from this check. Its text is about audit records across different repositories being analyzed for organization-wide situational awareness; a per-index retention parameter asserts nothing about analysis. It moves to scf.MON-06.log_reporting_capability.

checks.scope: Every CloudTrail trail in every connected AWS account. One row per trail, not one boolean per account.
data_sources: aws:cloudtrail.describe_trails (trailList) + a per-trail cloudtrail.get_trail_status fan-out — REQUIRES A NEW ROW-PRODUCING SWEEP IN cloud_transport.py, NOT a connector_checks resource. Verified: aws is the only one of 66 providers with no CONNECTOR_CHECKS entry (it declares transport:aws and has no base/verify), so evidence_engine cannot reach it. Model it on _iam_mfa_sweep in SWEEPS['aws']. get_trail_status clears _is_readonly_aws_operation (get_ prefix). Today CLOUD_CHECKS['aws']['aws.cloudtrail'] is one any_item_field_equals over trailList on IsMultiRegionTrail — one boolean, no rows, no population_size.
checks.assertion: sources:[{role:population, provider:aws, resource:trails, require:each_connected}] assert:{op:ALL, where:[["is_logging","truthy"],["is_multi_region","truthy"],["log_file_validation","truthy"]]} empty_population:fail
checks.evidence: One result per AWS connection. population_size = trail count, detail names each trail failing on which of the three fields. log_file_validation carries MON-08_A04 — nothing else in the catalog evidences log integrity. CEILING: LogFileValidationEnabled evidences tamper-DETECTION, not the access and deletion halves of MON-08_A04; those stay partly manual.
checks.not_applicable_when: No aws connection in scope. Never not_applicable for a connected account: zero trails is the finding (empty_population:fail), which the current any_item_field_equals cannot distinguish from a collection error. FIXED: MON-02.9_A01 removed — it asserts that a current and accurate inventory of technology assets being logged is maintained, and a trail-configuration test is not an asset inventory. Moved to unautomatable.

checks.scope: Org users on the log platform holding the Admin role — the people who can alter or delete logging configuration. Population filter is role eq Admin applied as a source scope, so the recorded denominator is the admin set, not all users.
data_sources: grafana:org_users — VERIFIED (path /api/org/users, fields email, login, role)
checks.assertion: sources:[{role:population, provider:grafana, resource:org_users, require:each_connected, scope:{where:[["role","eq","Admin"]]}}] assert:{op:COUNT, cmp:{lte:{param:"MON-08.2_A02", default:3}}} empty_population:fail
checks.evidence: population_size = admin count, detail lists admin emails. Replaces grafana.org_admins_limited (max_count 5, hardcoded, bound to CC6.1/CC6.3) with a parameterized threshold bound to the two objectives whose text is literally identical ('access to management of audit logging functionality is authorized to only a subset of privileged users or roles'). ENGINE GAP: lte is also new (see MON-02 note).
checks.not_applicable_when: Grafana not connected in scope. Zero admins is NOT not_applicable and NOT a pass — a real Grafana org always has at least one admin, so an empty result means a token without org:read, which empty_population:fail surfaces instead of hiding.

checks.scope: Log streams configured on the connected IdP. A tenant-buffered log that never leaves the IdP cannot evidence retained records of attempted use of deactivated accounts.
checks.assertion: sources:[{role:population, provider:auth0, resource:log_stream, require:named}] assert:{op:ANY, where:[["status","eq","active"]]} empty_population:fail
checks.evidence: population_size = configured streams, detail names the active stream(s) or reports zero. connector=auth0. Strictly stronger than the shipped auth0.log_stream_configured (min_count 1, CC7.2). CEILING: an active stream proves tenant logs are exported, not that the deactivated-account event type specifically is generated — the log_stream field map carries only name and status, no event filter. The A01 binding is a proxy, and must be labelled one.
checks.not_applicable_when: auth0 is not connected. Explicitly NOT satisfied by okta / google_workspace / microsoft_365 / jumpcloud being connected: verified, none of those four exposes any log, event or audit resource in its field map, so require:each_connected over category identity would mark them not_applicable and silently claim the domain is covered. Provider-scoped on purpose — and this is why the identity category semantics was corrected to evidence_provider.

checks.scope: Every active (non-paused) uptime/alert monitor, joined to the escalation policy it routes to. A monitor that fires into nothing does not alert personnel.
data_sources: better_stack:monitors — VERIFIED (fields name, url, monitor_type, status, paused from bool:attributes.paused_at, verify_ssl, policy_id)

better_stack:policies — fields name, repeat_count, steps (len:attributes.steps) VERIFIED; the join key is genuinely absent — REQUIRES adding "id":"id" to the policies field map. steps is already a count, so the gte 1 comparison works as written.
checks.assertion: sources:[{role:population, provider:better_stack, resource:monitors, require:named, scope:{where:[["paused","falsy"]]}},{role:evidence, provider:better_stack, resource:policies, require:named}] join:{on:["policy_id","id"], unmatched_left:"fail", unmatched_right:"ignore", zero_matches:"error"} assert:{op:ALL, where:[["@evidence.steps","gte",1]]} empty_population:fail
checks.evidence: population_size = active monitors, join_quality (matched / unmatched-left / unmatched-right) in detail, sources[] records both roles. unmatched_left:fail IS the control — a monitor with a null or dangling policy_id is the violation and an inner join would delete it. CEILING: these are uptime monitors; MON-01.12_A04 is about activities with cybersecurity implications, so this evidences the routing half (an alert reaches a human on a policy with at least one step), not the detection half.
checks.not_applicable_when: better_stack not connected. FIXED — empty_population changed from not_applicable to fail. The submitted spec deferred the empty case to 'scf.MON-01.2.*', but no better_stack check exists in this set (the MON-01.2 pair is signoz and datadog) and the shipped better_stack.monitors_present binds A1.1, not any MON objective — so the zero-active-monitors gap was assigned to a check that does not exist and would have read as covered. FIXED: MON-01.4_A05 removed — it names system-generated compromise indicators, which an uptime monitor does not produce.

checks.scope: Every alert rule defined in SigNoz. Sibling spec to scf.MON-01.2.datadog_monitors_notify_no_data — same objective, different provider, because resource names diverge (signoz 'rules' vs datadog 'monitors') and one source entry carries one resource name.
data_sources: signoz:rules — VERIFIED (path /api/v2/rules, items:[data], fields alert, state, disabled, id)
checks.assertion: sources:[{role:population, provider:signoz, resource:rules, require:each_connected}] assert:{op:ALL, where:[["disabled","falsy"]]} empty_population:fail
checks.evidence: population_size = rule count, detail names each disabled rule. Per-ao roll-up over both siblings: any FAIL on MON-01.2_A01 fails the objective before the control roll-up runs.
checks.not_applicable_when: signoz not connected. Zero rules on a connected SigNoz is empty_population:fail. The disagreement the spec cites is CONFIRMED in evidence_engine._eval_check: min_count keeps its arithmetic on an empty set (signoz.alert_rules_present fails at 0) while every offender-list kind — all_true/all_false/none_match/all_match/present — returns not_run on an empty set by design. So the two shipped checks genuinely disagree on the same empty population, and empty_population:fail is the resolution.

checks.scope: Datadog metric-alert monitors. notify_no_data is the property that makes a monitor detect the ABSENCE of telemetry, which is the near-real-time-analysis claim rather than 'a monitor object exists'. Scoped to type eq 'metric alert' — see the fix note.
data_sources: datadog:monitors — VERIFIED (path /monitor, fields name, type, id, notify_no_data from options.notify_no_data)
checks.assertion: sources:[{role:population, provider:datadog, resource:monitors, require:each_connected, scope:{where:[["type","eq","metric alert"]]}}] assert:{op:ALL, where:[["notify_no_data","truthy"]]} empty_population:fail
checks.evidence: population_size = metric-alert monitors, detail names those that will stay silent when their source stops reporting. Strictly stronger than the shipped datadog.monitors_configured (min_count 1).
checks.not_applicable_when: datadog not connected in scope. FIXED: added the type scope. Unscoped, ALL notify_no_data truthy over every monitor fails in essentially every real tenant — composite, event, log and service-check monitors routinely and correctly leave notify_no_data off, so the unscoped assertion is a permanent red that carries no information, which is as useless as one that always passes.

checks.scope: Population = managed endpoints from Kandji (the asset system of record). Evidence = EDR agents from the security vendor. Devices flagged missing are excluded from the denominator; a device the MDM has lost contact with is a different control.
data_sources: kandji:devices — VERIFIED (fields device_id, name from device_name, platform, os_version, mdm from mdm_enabled, agent from agent_installed, missing from is_missing) — population
sentinelone:agents — VERIFIED (fields name from raw.computerName, active from raw.isActive, uptodate from raw.isUpToDate, encrypted, firewall, version) — evidence
checks.assertion: sources:[{role:population, provider:kandji, resource:devices, require:each_connected, scope:{where:[["missing","falsy"]]}},{role:evidence, provider:sentinelone, resource:agents, require:named}] join:{on:["name","name"], unmatched_left:"fail", unmatched_right:"ignore", zero_matches:"error"} assert:{op:ALL, where:[["@evidence.active","truthy"],["@evidence.uptodate","truthy"]]} empty_population:not_applicable
checks.evidence: population_size from Kandji, evidence provenance in the new sources[] column — VERIFIED that SCFCheckResult has no such column today (it has connector, connection_id, credential_fingerprint, granted_scopes) and connector alone cannot express two providers. KNOWN CEILING CONFIRMED: joining on hostname because neither kandji.devices nor jamf.computers collects a serial number; kandji serial_number and jamf GENERAL.serialNumber must be added before this join is trustworthy. Until then report join_quality and treat a high unmatched_left rate as a key problem, not a fleet of unprotected laptops.
checks.not_applicable_when: kandji not connected, or it returns zero non-missing devices. If kandji is connected but sentinelone is not, the result is ERROR not not_applicable: the population exists and the property is untested. FIXED: check id suffixed .kandji — the submitted spec's not_applicable_when said 'no mdm connector connected' while its source named kandji alone, so a jamf-only tenant would have been marked not_applicable while the mdm category claimed population coverage. The jamf sibling is now authored explicitly below.

checks.scope: ADDED. Identical assertion, jamf as the population. The spec argued (correctly, for signoz/datadog) that one source entry carries one resource name, then relied on a jamf sibling it never wrote — this is it.
data_sources: jamf:computers — VERIFIED (path /api/v1/computers-inventory?section=GENERAL&SECURITY&DISK_ENCRYPTION; fields name from raw.general.name, last_contact, fv_enabled, gatekeeper, sip, firewall) — population
checks.assertion: sources:[{role:population, provider:jamf, resource:computers, require:each_connected},{role:evidence, provider:sentinelone, resource:agents, require:named}] join:{on:["name","name"], unmatched_left:"fail", unmatched_right:"ignore", zero_matches:"error"} assert:{op:ALL, where:[["@evidence.active","truthy"],["@evidence.uptodate","truthy"]]} empty_population:not_applicable
checks.evidence: population_size from Jamf. Two ceilings, both verified in the field map: (1) same hostname-join weakness, and worse here because jamf.computers has no is_missing equivalent — only last_contact — so a long-decommissioned machine stays in the denominator until a last_contact staleness scope is added; (2) sentinelone.agents keys on raw.computerName, which matches Jamf's general.name only by convention.
checks.not_applicable_when: jamf not connected, or zero computers returned. jamf connected without sentinelone is ERROR, not not_applicable.

checks.scope: Audit records in the user/group/permission categories from the connected work platform, over the parameterized lookback window.
data_sources: jira:audit_records — VERIFIED (path /auditing/record?limit=1000, fields summary, category, created, author from authorKey). Scan of all 66 connectors confirms it is the only event-shaped resource whose field map retains a timestamp.
checks.assertion: sources:[{role:population, provider:jira, resource:audit_records, require:each_connected, scope:{where:[["category","in",["user management","group management","permissions"]]]}}] assert:{op:ANY, where:[["created","age_lt_days",{param:"MON-16.4_A01", default:90}]]} empty_population:fail
checks.evidence: population_size = matching records in the window, tested_size = same, truncated=true when the window is saturated. Two truncation limits, both confirmed and both must be recorded: the path hardcodes limit=1000 AND evidence_engine caps every resource at MAX_ITEMS=300, so a busy tenant is always truncated — and SCFCheckResult's own comment says truncated=True can never yield satisfactory. ENGINE GAP: age_lt_days is new (the `in` operator already exists in _op).
checks.not_applicable_when: jira not connected. Zero matching records is empty_population:fail, not not_applicable: in a tenant with any admin activity, an empty privileged-change feed means the filter categories are wrong for this Jira version or the audit scope is off — both need a human, neither is a pass. FIXED: MON-03_A03 removed — it says audit records CONTAIN information establishing when the event occurred, which is a record-content property, not a feed-freshness property; an ANY-is-recent assertion passes on a feed where most records carry no usable stamp. It moves to scf.MON-07.audit_timestamps_utc_parseable, whose ALL-records regex assertion actually evidences it.

checks.scope: Every collected audit record. A record-content test: the population IS the evidence, and the assertion is about completeness of the record, not about a system setting. No new API call — it re-reads rows already collected for jira.audit_logging_active.
checks.assertion: sources:[{role:population, provider:jira, resource:audit_records, require:each_connected}] assert:{op:ALL, where:[["author","truthy"]]} empty_population:not_applicable
checks.evidence: population_size = records examined, detail counts and samples records with a null actor. The cheapest check in the domain and the only thing evidencing the MON-03 record-content family at all.
checks.not_applicable_when: jira not connected, or the audit endpoint returns zero records (nothing was examined, so nothing can be asserted — the correct use of the not_applicable default, unlike the MON-16.4 freshness sibling where emptiness is itself the signal; and the empty case is not silently green because the shipped jira.audit_logging_active min_count 1 fails on it). FIXED: MON-03_A05 removed — it asserts records establish the SOURCE of the event (the component that generated it), which authorKey is not; no connector collects an event source field, so A05 moves to unautomatable.

checks.scope: ADDED. The submitted spec named confluence as a 'sibling spec, identical assertion' inside the jira check's data_sources and never authored it, which would have left every Confluence tenant untested while appearing covered.
data_sources: confluence:audit — VERIFIED (path /audit, fields category, summary, author from author.displayName, sysAdmin). Note: no timestamp is retained, so this resource can carry the actor-identity test but NOT the MON-07 format test or the MON-16.4 freshness test.
checks.assertion: sources:[{role:population, provider:confluence, resource:audit, require:each_connected}] assert:{op:ALL, where:[["author","truthy"]]} empty_population:not_applicable
checks.evidence: population_size = records examined, detail samples records with a null actor. connector=confluence.
checks.not_applicable_when: confluence not connected, or /audit returns zero records. The empty case is covered by the shipped confluence.audit_log_active (min_count 1).

checks.scope: Datadog monitors of type 'log alert' — monitors that watch the logging pipeline itself rather than the application.
data_sources: datadog:monitors — VERIFIED (fields name, type, id, notify_no_data); confirmed the field map exposes NO tags key
checks.assertion: sources:[{role:population, provider:datadog, resource:monitors, require:named}] assert:{op:ANY, where:[["type","eq","log alert"],["notify_no_data","truthy"]]} empty_population:fail
checks.evidence: detail names the qualifying monitor(s). KNOWN CEILING: proves a log-type monitor exists that alerts on absent data, not that it watches logging-process failure specifically. The exact version needs a tenant tag convention (scope where tags contains {param:'log_pipeline_tag', default:'compliance:log-pipeline'}); confirmed the datadog monitors field map has no tags field — a one-line field-map addition, not an API gap.
checks.not_applicable_when: datadog not connected in scope. Zero monitors of any kind is empty_population:fail. FIXED: MON-05.2_A04 removed — it requires a warning when allocated event-log storage volume reaches a defined percentage of capacity, and nothing in datadog:log_indexes carries volume, quota or daily-limit (the field map keeps name and retention_days only). Moved to unautomatable.

checks.scope: Every collected audit record's timestamp field. Asserts the format half of the objective (UTC, or an explicit fixed offset carried in the stamp) — not the clock-synchronization half.
data_sources: jira:audit_records — VERIFIED (field created). Provider-scoped: confluence.audit and servicenow sys_audit drop their timestamps, so no sibling is possible for this one.
checks.assertion: sources:[{role:population, provider:jira, resource:audit_records, require:each_connected}] assert:{op:ALL, where:[["created","matches","^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}T.*(Z|[+-]\\d{2}:?\\d{2})$"]]} empty_population:not_applicable
checks.evidence: population_size = records examined, detail samples any record whose stamp carries no offset. ENGINE GAP: `matches` is new. This is the only automatable slice of MON-07 — MON-07_A02 and MON-07.1_A01/A02/A03/A05 stay manual because no connector exposes NTP configuration or clock offset. CEILING: MON-07_A01 also demands an organization-defined granularity of time measurement; the regex evidences the offset half only. FIXED: MON-03_A03 added here, moved off the MON-16.4 freshness check — an ALL-records assertion that every stamp parses is exactly 'records contain information that establishes when the event occurred'.
checks.not_applicable_when: jira not connected, or zero audit records collected.

checks.scope: Every device present on the connected overlay network. Detects nodes that joined without approval and nodes shared in from a foreign tailnet.
data_sources: tailscale:devices — VERIFIED (path /tailnet/-/devices, fields name, hostname, os, user, key_expiry_disabled, update_available, authorized, external from isExternal)
checks.assertion: sources:[{role:population, provider:tailscale, resource:devices, require:each_connected}] assert:{op:ALL, where:[["authorized","truthy"],["external","falsy"]]} empty_population:not_applicable
checks.evidence: population_size = tailnet nodes, detail names each unauthorized or externally-shared node. Rebinds the existing tailscale.device_authorized (CC6.1) onto the unauthorized-connection objectives it actually evidences.
